redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_stamp_verification.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 2 of 266 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - si5 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 263/266 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: stamp-verification.py: added _lf (CRLF->LF) applied in both _head_text and _wt_text so the hunk split and changed_source compare line content in one newline form; added _in_endings_of and _isolated_run now writes an inline suite's test-only copy in the line ends the throwaway's file (HEAD's blob) already uses. Tests: replaced si5/si6 with si5 (LF blob vs CRLF wt, autocrlf=true), si6 (CRLF vs CRLF), si7 (LF vs LF), each through a real git repo asserting exact hunk split (1 held, 1 applied) and changed_source True for the edit / False for an unchanged copy; si8 pins write-back line ends. Own selftest run: 266/266 passed, exit 0; ruff clean.
outcome.descriptive: An inline suite and a declared source compare by line content, so Windows autocrlf checkouts no longer see whole-file hunks or phantom changed sources.
